---
title: "Recipe: ride a release without breaking pinned tooling"
toc-title: Recipe
---

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Tool | kailash (flake update / nixos-rebuild) |
| Section | Administrator |
| Level | medium |
| Time | ~30 min |
| Layer/Category | admin (whole-system) |
| Tags | `admin`, `updates`, `release`, `reproducibility` |


## Problem

A Kailash installation never updates anything in the background — no
package re-links, no tool moves, no lock drift. The other side: the
operator wants a newer release only deliberately. The update carries
no surprise breakage. The operator names what moved before the
switch. The documentation keeps pace with the pins it describes.

## Solution

Pull the lock delta. Review what moved. Rebuild. Verify — on the
operator's own cadence:

```bash
# 1. Record where you are now
nix flake metadata github:kailash-os/kailash-os/2026.01-alpha.1 | head -5
nix profile list 2>/dev/null | head -5   # or your system's current generation

# 2. Update your host's lock (the review point — nothing moves yet)
nix flake update

# 3. See exactly what the delta moves before building
nix flake lock --update-input kailash-packages   # scoped, or the full bump
nix --profile diff-closures /run/current-system \
    "$(nix build --no-link --print-out-paths .#nixosConfigurations.<host>.config.system.build.toplevel)"

# 4. Rebuild and switch
sudo nixos-rebuild switch

# 5. Verify the declared build state
kailash manifest validate
```

What success looks like:

- the diff-closures step names the versions that moved
  (up/down/changed) BEFORE anything switches
- no surprise rides the apply step
- `nixos-rebuild switch` completes. The boot entry for the previous
  generation remains — rollback is a reboot away
- `kailash manifest validate` is green after the switch
- the release naming holds: `2026.01` → staged `2026.02-alpha.1` →
  `2026.02` GA
- a material same-month re-cut is dotted `2026.01.1`
- a staged cut carries the suffix honestly (`git tag -v` shows it),
  and the bare name stays reserved for GA

## Discussion

- **The lockfile is the version:** rolling changes merge on main
  between releases. A system pinned to last month's lock keeps
  rebuilding it reproducibly, until its operator deliberately pulls
  a newer one. A build against the same lock reproduces the
  identical tool set. That is why "the version" is a fact, not an
  impression.
- **Two ways to move forward:** rebuild against a newer lock at the
  operator's own cadence, or adopt a released lock bump as-is.
  Either way the move is a review, not a countdown.
- **Documentation rides the pin:** every guide man-page carries the
  exact pinned version it was written against, and every recipe here
  carries a provenance footer. A moving pin without a regeneration
  is a red-regenerate event, enforced by CI (the guide's gate; the
  book's gate lane mirrors it) — the docs never silently disagree
  with the system.
- **Fast-moving tools:** pins are re-checked on class-based cadences
  (weekly fast-moving, fortnightly steady, nixpkgs monthly). A
  check becomes a PR only when the smoke check passes. Merge is
  human-approved.
- **Rollback posture:** generations mean an update that disappoints
  is restarted, not untangled. Boot the previous generation, then
  revisit the lock delta.
